title: How small a water-main leak can pressure sensors find, and does a changepoint detector beat a threshold or CUSUM?
lede: Water-leak detection on EPANET's Net3 (WNTR) at a 5% weekly false-alarm budget: with 10% demand error, CUSUM on 5 pressure sensors finds 92% of visible leaks at 4% of demand and 46% at 2%, but only 28% of locations are visible even to all 92 junctions; a flow balance on the inflow meter finds every 4% leak when demand is well known (simulated leaks; BattLeDIM L-Town was unreachable).
summary: WNTR simulates one week of hourly pressures and inflow on EPANET’s Net3 (92 junctions) with leaks of 0.25–4 % of mean demand (1.7–28 L/s) opened at hour 96 at 60 random junctions, against a nominal model whose demands are wrong (node error sd 5–20 %, system-wide AR(1) error sd 1–5 %) and pressure sensors with noise 0.05–1 m. A moving-average threshold, CUSUM and PELT (changepoint) each get a threshold calibrated on 120 leak-free weeks to at most 5 % of weeks with any alarm, on pressure residuals, on pressure regressed on a noisy inflow meter, and on the inflow residual alone (a flow balance). With 5 sensors, base demand error and 0.25 m noise, CUSUM finds 92 % of the leaks the sensors can see at 4 % of demand, 46 % at 2 % and 8 % at 1 %. Only 28 % of locations are visible above 0.5 m, and that holds even with all 92 junctions as sensors: in Net3 tanks and pumps hold the pressures. The flow balance needs no pressure sensor and is best when demand is well known (low error: 100 % of 4 % leaks and 62 % of 2 % leaks anywhere, against 52 % and 30 % for pressure) but no better at base or high error. Demand error moves every result far more than sensor noise. PELT did not beat CUSUM on 2 % leaks in any condition. Corrected 2026-11-23: an earlier version’s inflow meter could not see the leak, which inflated the flow-adjusted results (85 % at 2 %). Limits: BattLeDIM L-Town could not be downloaded, so there is no comparison with the competition’s methods; Net3 is a textbook network; leaks are simulated with a fixed orifice exponent of 0.5; demand error and meter noise (0.5 %) are assumed and swept, not measured; 60 locations per size, so rates carry binomial error of up to ±0.12.
